instruction: Look at dome_pocket.step in SOLIDWORKS with the SOLIDWORKS CAM add-in. Create a 3-axis roughing toolpath for dome_pocket.step using any available standard 3-axis roughing, area-clearance, or pocket-style operation, then create a finishing toolpath for the spherical region using any available ball-end finishing strategy such as contour, parallel, scallop, Z-level, HSM, or HSS. 3D iMachining or HSR may be used only if it is available, but it is not required. Roughing must leave 0.3 mm stock and finishing must target zero stock. Use standard roughing and finishing operations and keep SOLIDWORKS CAM's default generated NC comments; do not rename operations just to add labels. Do not force exact tool station numbers, spindle speeds, feedrates, or internal tool-library IDs if SOLIDWORKS CAM's Technology Database assigns stable defaults; use suitable installed tool-library entries for the required operation types and let the posted NC program reflect those real CAM selections. Save the required output file(s) to the Desktop: C:\Users\User\Desktop\task-15.nc. Generate the required NC/G-code file(s) by using SOLIDWORKS CAM's normal Post Process workflow after calculating the toolpath, with an installed .ctl postprocessor from C:\ProgramData\SOLIDWORKS\SOLIDWORKS CAM 2025\Posts. For milling tasks, prefer m3axis-tutorial.ctl, mach_iii.ctl, or haas_vf3.ctl; for turning tasks, use an installed turning .ctl post such as fanuc_t2axis.ctl. If the generated program opens in NC Editor or is initially saved with a different extension, use Save As from that generated program to save the exact requested Desktop filename(s). Do not manually write, fabricate, or directly create the NC/G-code text outside SOLIDWORKS CAM. You must complete all operations interactively through the graphical user interface (GUI) step by step. The use of external script files is strictly prohibited.
